column2: Judah's divisions, Idumea, wilderness of Zin and Kadesh toward the southwest follow the selected opening; no lot clause imported.
Salt Sea edge and projecting ridge retain the two southwestern relations; ridge is the inherited rendering of lophia.
Present boundary verbs run through Akrabin, Senna, Kadesh-barnea, Hezron and Addara before the western Kadesh circuit. Selected forms are not replaced with another boundary list.
Present approach to Azmon changes to future passage and termination; the inherited stages preserve this shift and the Egyptian ravine.
The entire Salt Sea reaches the Jordan on the east; the northern description starts separately with sea ridge and Jordan edge.
Beth-hoglah, northern Beth-arabah and the stone of Baion son of Reuben remain in order; Baion is not silently normalized to Bohan.
The fourth part of Achor, descent to Gilgal and Addamin's southwestern relation remain. Future passage and ending distinguish the last two clauses.
column3: The unusual fourth-part expression and the geographical attachment of southwest require specialist assessment; no Debir reading substituted.

column2: Onom, the southwestern Jebus ridge, the explicit Jerusalem identification and the mountain facing the ravine toward the sea remain; Raphain's northern relation is not flattened.
The two present passage verbs are followed by future exaxei. Change leads to will lead to preserve this selected shift, retaining Naphtho, Ephron and Baal's Jearim identification.
Future circuit, passage, descent and passage remain throughout; Mount Assares, ridge, northern Jearim/Chesalon and City of the Sun retain the selected order.
column3: The exact attachment of the ridge and city phrases is difficult; inherited punctuation is provisional, not a geographical identification.

column2: Northern Ekron ridge, Shikkeron, Mount Baalah and Jabneel lead to the sea in future verbs, without inserting a different boundary endpoint.
The western heading and future Great Sea boundary are both retained; the closing statement returns to Judah's divisions all around.
Both giving clauses, God's command, Joshua's explicit name and Arbok as Anak's mother-city remain; the description is not changed to a great man.
Destruction is attributed to Caleb son of Jephunneh; Sousi, Talmai and Achima represent the three named sons of Anak in this selected list.
Caleb ascends against Debir's inhabitants; the former name is translated City of Letters, matching grammata rather than introducing an untranslated alternate name.
Taking, cutting down and gaining mastery remain three coordinated actions before the offer of Achsah as wife; none is collapsed into capture alone.
Othniel son of Kenaz, the younger-brother description and the giving of Achsah are retained without reassigning the kinship in the running text.
column3: The attachment of Caleb's younger brother needs a kinship note: the Greek nominative apposition favors Othniel; inherited English may also be read as referring to Kenaz.

column2: Achsah consults with him and herself says I will ask my father; she cries from the donkey. No dismounting or urging the husband to ask is imported.
The blessing request, gift to the land of Negeb and named Golathmaim are retained, including separate Upper and Lower grants; no water-springs paraphrase replaces the names.
The short Judah inheritance notice closes the Caleb episode without importing an additional family-division phrase.
First city, Edom and wilderness frame Kaibaiseleel, Ara and Hazor. The selected combined first name is retained rather than split into other traditions' cities.
Ikam, Regma and Arouel remain the three selected names and their order.
Kedesh and the single selected form Asorionain remain two entries; the latter is not split into a familiar longer list.
Mainam and Balmainan retain their attached villages clause within the continuing list.
The plural cities of Aseron and singular identification that is Hazor are both retained, without silently repairing their number difference.
Sen, Salmaa and Moladah retain the selected three-place sequence.
Seri and Baiphalad remain two entries, without supplementation from a different city list.
Cholaseola and Beer-sheba retain both villages and settlements; the distinct settlement terms are not merged.
Baalah, Bakok and Asom retain their order and distinct identities.
Elboudad, Bethel and Hormah remain the selected sequence; Bethel is not replaced by a more familiar southern name.
Ziklag, Macharim and Sethennak remain three listed names without harmonization.
Labos, Sale and Eromoth are followed by the selected total twenty-nine and villages. The printed total remains even though the visible named expressions can be counted differently.
column3: Counting one entry per named expression in 15:21-32 gives thirty, including the cities of Aseron as one. The selected twenty-nine is retained; the discrepancy and plural expression need apparatus/geographical review.

column2: The plain heading precedes Eshtaol, Raa and Assa; the latter two are not replaced with familiar alternatives.
Ramen, Tano, Ilouthoth and Maiani supply four entries, preserving the selected longer line.
Jarmuth, Adullam, Membra, Socoh and Azekah supply five entries; Membra remains rather than being omitted to match another list.
Sakarim and Gederah complete fourteen entries in 15:33-36. Its settlements attaches singularly to Gederah before the total and plural villages.
Senna, Adasan and Magadagad begin the next city group in the selected order.
Dalal, Mizpah and Jakareel remain the three selected entries.
Lachish, Basedoth and Ideadalea retain their forms without identifying them with differently divided names elsewhere.
Chabra, Maches and Maachos remain three distinct entries despite the similar final two names.
Geddor, Bagadiel, Naamah and Makkedah complete the selected sixteen-entry group, followed by villages.
Libnah and Ithak begin the next group with two entries, without supplying another city.
Anoch, Jana and Nezib continue the selected three-name sequence.
Keilam, Akiezi, Kezib, Bathesar and Ailon bring this group to ten; both similar Akiezi/Kezib names are retained.
Ekron has its villages and their settlements: the singular-to-plural possessive shift in the selected Greek is preserved.
From Ekron, Gemna and all places near Ashdod retain the selected formulation and villages; Gemna is not converted into a directional phrase.
column3: The attachment of from Ekron to Gemna is compressed in Greek; inherited coordination remains provisional.

column2: Ashdod and Gaza each retain villages and settlements; the Egyptian torrent and Great Sea boundary close the coastal sequence.
The hill-country heading precedes Shamir, Jattir and Socoh, preserving the regional transition.
Renna and City of Letters remain two entries, with Debir explicitly identified as the latter.
Anon, Eskaiman and Aisam retain the three selected names.
Gosom, Chalou and Channa complete eleven entries in 15:48-51; villages remains the selected settlement term.
Airem, Remna and Soma begin the next three-name sequence; Remna is not silently identified with Renna above.
Jemain, Bethachou and Phakoua remain the next three entries.
Euma, Arbok/Hebron and Sorth complete nine entries; the closing term settlements remains distinct from villages elsewhere.
Maor, Carmel, Ozib and Itan begin the next group with four entries.
Jariel, Jarikam and Zakanaiim remain three distinct selected names.
Gibeah and Timnah complete nine entries in this group, followed by villages.
Aloua, Beth-zur and Geddon begin the next group without substituting names from another witness.
Magaroth, Bethanam and Thekoum complete six entries, with villages. Thekoum is not merged with the following Tekoa entry.
The full selected eleven-city list remains as a separate lettered unit: Tekoa, Ephrathah/Bethlehem, Phagor, Aitan, Koulon, Tatam, Eobes, Karem, Galem, Thether and Manocho, with villages.
Kiriath-baal/Jearim and Sotheba remain two entries with settlements; the alias is not counted as a third city.
Baddargis, Tharabaam, Ainon and Aichioza remain four entries; no wilderness heading is added where this selected line does not give one.
Naphlazon, the cities of Sodom and Ankades conclude with seven cities and villages; the plural cities expression is retained.
column3: The seven total counts the Sodom expression as one list item, although that expression is plural; retain both without claiming a resolved geographical count.

column2: Judah's inability to destroy the Jebusites and their continued residence in Jerusalem remain. The selected temporal ending is until that day, not until this day.
